title: Coast Guard Rescues All 20 Crew From Grounded Cargo Ship Off Andhra Coast
excerpt: ICG Ship Sujay and a helicopter airlifted the crew of the MV Sigma Pearl off Antarvedi after Cyclone Arnab, completing the high-risk rescue within 24 hours with zero loss of life at sea.
body:
• The Indian Coast Guard rescued all 20 crew members from the Marshall Islands-flagged bulk carrier MV Sigma Pearl, which ran aground off Antarvedi on the Andhra Pradesh coast after Cyclone Arnab.
  • ICG Ship Sujay and a Coast Guard helicopter airlifted the crew in rough seas, using the helipad at Mogalthur village in West Godavari district, completing the operation within 24 hours with zero loss of life at sea.
  • The Singapore-bound vessel had left Visakhapatnam at 12.17 a.m. on October 27 after unloading cargo, and suffered engine failure while navigating through the Ravva oilfield.
  • Authorities are now assessing the grounded ship for salvage and monitoring for pollution, as it carries furnace oil and possibly marine diesel aboard.

The Indian Coast Guard rescued all 20 crew members from a Singapore-bound cargo ship stranded off the Andhra Pradesh coast on Thursday, in a high-risk operation carried out in rough seas after very severe cyclone Arnab. The Coast Guard said it safely rescued all 20 crew from the aground vessel MV Sigma Pearl off Antarvedi, deploying its ship Sujay and a helicopter to airlift those trapped on the merchant ship, according to IANS.

How the rescue unfolded

The bulk carrier, sailing under the Marshall Islands flag, was stranded near Antarvedi while navigating through the Ravva oilfield due to engine failure, suspected to have occurred under the impact of severe cyclonic storm Arnab in the Bay of Bengal. The vessel's master sent out an SOS after onboard efforts to free the ship failed. On receiving the communication, the Coast Guard launched an operation and completed it within 24 hours, safely rescuing all the crew members.

https://x.com/IndiaCoastGuard/status/2115813696887005444

Coast Guard personnel used the helipad at Mogalthur village in West Godavari district for the rescue efforts. Nation Press reported the 179.90-metre bulk carrier ran aground following high seas and powerful winds as Cyclone Arnab made landfall along the Andhra coast early on Wednesday, and that preemptive coastal monitoring and Disaster Response Team deployments were credited with ensuring zero loss of life at sea.

The ship and its voyage

The MV Sigma Pearl is a bulk carrier registered under the Marshall Islands flag, with a deadweight of 32,688 tonnes. It suffered engine failure while returning to Singapore after unloading cargo at Visakhapatnam port. The vessel departed Visakhapatnam port around 12.17 a.m. on October 27, around the time Cyclone Arnab was approaching Yanam before making landfall in the early hours of October 28.

Officials noted that while the ship was likely not carrying cargo at the time of grounding, it would have had furnace oil and possibly marine diesel on board. Authorities are in contact with the ship's management and owners to arrange salvage operations, and the vessel's condition is still being assessed.

Cyclone Arnab's wider damage

Very severe cyclonic storm Arnab crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast in the early hours of October 28 with maximum sustained wind speed of 125-135 kmph, gusting up to 150 kmph, according to the India Meteorological Department. The process continued for six hours till 8 a.m. The cyclone claimed seven lives on land, leaving a trail of destruction in coastal districts, uprooting thousands of trees and electricity poles and causing extensive damage to crops.

The Coast Guard had initiated precautionary steps ahead of landfall, including coastal monitoring and Disaster Response Team deployment along the Andhra coast. Fishermen were directed to remain ashore, and continuous maritime surveillance was maintained to identify stranded vessels. On the same day, a Coast Guard helicopter also conducted rescue operations in flood-affected areas of Odisha.

What happens next

With the crew safe, attention turns to the grounded vessel itself. The Coast Guard is India's nodal agency for combating marine pollution in its Exclusive Economic Zone, and with fuel oil aboard the Sigma Pearl, authorities are closely monitoring for any risk of an oil spill along the Andhra coastline while salvage coordination with the ship's owners continues.
